Univariate analysis identifies that sex differences are greatest in association networks. We fit a generalised additive model (GAM) at each vertex to determine the impact of sex on network loadings. Site, age and motion were included as covariates, with age modelled using a penalised spline and site modelled as a random effect. Support vector machine (SVM) models classify participant sex based on personalised functional network (PFN) topography. SVMs were trained with nested, twofold cross-validation (2F-CV) to classify participants’ sex (male or female) from PFN functional topography.
